heading: INT. MUSEUM OF CLOCKS - GALLERY OF AUTOMATA - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MUSEUM OF CLOCKS - GALLERY OF AUTOMATA - NIGHT
A hushed gallery lined with glass cases.
Hundreds of clocks tick out of rhythm: cuckoos, carriage clocks, a grandfather the height of a wardrobe.
A mechanical bird in a gilt cage sings once an hour.
Moonlight pools on parquet.
At the center, five people in museum staff blazers pretend to inspect a display.
They are not staff.
MADAME ODETTE FONTAINE-ABARA, 60s, silver chignon, holds a tiny silver wand like a baton and speaks as if lecturing an audience.
THADDEUS "TICK" WILLOUGHBY, 30s, with a tool roll under his blazer, crouches at the grandfather clock.
LOTTIE PAXTON, 20s, in sneakers, unspools a coil of fishing line.
OLD BERTRAM MULDOON, 70s, with a cane and a hearing aid, taps a case with one knuckle.
And JOSEFINA "JOJO" ARRIAGA, 30s, the lookout, stands in the arched doorway pretending to read a pamphlet.
And here we have the Marquis automaton, circa 1782, a marvel of pre-Revolutionary engineering.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: She does the voice every time.
units.name: TICK

units.text: It's the voice that makes it work.
units.name: LOTTIE

units.text: Bertram knocks on the glass of the automaton's case and cups a hand behind his ear.
A tiny gear inside shifts.
He nods, satisfied.

Lottie drops the fishing line through a crack in the display, feeds it down to the latch, and ties a knot in one smooth motion, while Tick unscrews the clock's back panel, reaches in, and removes a small velvet pouch.
Jojo, without looking up from her pamphlet, taps twice on the doorframe.
Everyone freezes.
Footsteps echo from the far corridor, then fade.
Clear.
units.name: JOJO

units.text: Note the delicate wrist articulation.
units.name: ODETTE

units.text: The mechanical bird begins to sing.
All five heads turn.
They stand, perfectly still, until it finishes its song.
